questions.text: Which bones form the medial margin of the orbital opening?

questions.modelAnswer: A small projection on the lower border of the fissure
questions.explanation: Model answer is provided based on the Special Senses syllabus.

questions.text: List the intrinsic muscles of the eye

questions.text: List the extrinsic muscles of the eye

questions.text: Which structures lie outside the orbital periosteum?
questions.modelAnswer: 1. Zygomatic nerve 2. Infraorbital nerve and vessels
questions.explanation: Model answer is provided based on the Special Senses syllabus.

questions.text: Where is the apex of the orbit located?
questions.modelAnswer: At the medial end of the superior orbital fissure

questions.text: The supraorbital notch/foramen is located at the junction of the ___ and ___ of the superior margin.
questions.explanation:
**Completed Sentence:**
The supraorbital notch/foramen is located at the junction of the **medial 1/3** and **lateral 2/3** of the superior margin.

questions.text: The ___ lies anterolaterally in the roof and lodges the ___.
questions.explanation:
The Lacrimal Fossa is a part of the Frontal Bone and is Foo2

**Completed Sentence:**
The **lacrimal fossa** lies anterolaterally in the roof and lodges the **lacrimal gland**.

questions.text: The optic canal lies at the junction of the ___ and ___ posteriorly.
questions.explanation:
**Completed Sentence:**
The optic canal lies at the junction of the **roof** and **medial wall** posteriorly.

questions.text: The optic canal transmits the ___ and the ___.
questions.explanation:
This is a suprior view of the orbit.

**Completed Sentence:**
The optic canal transmits the **optic nerve** and the **ophthalmic artery**.

questions.text: The ___ lies anteromedially on the roof and provides attachment for the pulley of the ___ muscle.
questions.explanation:
Superior view of the anterior cranial fossa

**Completed Sentence:**
The **trochlear fossa** lies anteromedially on the roof and provides attachment for the pulley of the **superior oblique** muscle.

questions.text: The superior orbital fissure lies at the junction of the ___ and ___ posteriorly.
questions.explanation:
**Completed Sentence:**
The superior orbital fissure lies at the junction of the **roof** and **lateral wall** posteriorly.

questions.text: The ___ part of the superior orbital fissure transmits the ___, ___, and ___ nerves.
questions.explanation:
LFT SNIA

**Completed Sentence:**
The **lateral** part of the superior orbital fissure transmits the **Lacrimal**, **Frontal**, and **Trochlear** nerves.

questions.text: The ___ part of the ___ fissure transmits the ___ and ___ nerves and ___ nerve.
questions.explanation:
LFT SNIA Within the tendinous ring

**Completed Sentence:**
The **middle** part of the **superior orbital** fissure transmits the **Oculomotor (III) (superior and inferior divisions** and **Abducent (VI)** nerves and **Nasociliary** nerve.

questions.text: The ___ part of the superior orbital fissure transmits the ___ and ___.
questions.explanation:
Within the tendinous ring

**Completed Sentence:**
The **medial** part of the superior orbital fissure transmits the **inferior ophthalmic vein** and **sympathetic nerves**.

questions.text: The inferior orbital fissure lies at the junction of the ___ and ___.
questions.explanation:
**Completed Sentence:**
The inferior orbital fissure lies at the junction of the **floor** and **lateral wall**.

questions.text: The orbit communicates with the ___ fossa ___ and the ___ fossa ___ via ___ fissure.
questions.explanation:
Communications of Pterygopalatine Fossa

**Completed Sentence:**
The orbit communicates with the **infratemporal** fossa **anteriorly** and the **pterygopalatine** fossa **posteriorly** via **the inferior orbital** fissure.

questions.text: The ___ nerve is a continuation of the ___ nerve and passes through the ___.
questions.explanation:
**Completed Sentence:**
The **infraorbital** nerve is a continuation of the **maxillary (V2)** nerve and passes through the **inferior orbital fissure**.

questions.text: The ___ lies anteriorly on the medial wall and lodges the ___.
questions.explanation:
Lacrimal Groove is a part of the Lacrimal Bone.

**Completed Sentence:**
The **lacrimal groove** lies anteriorly on the medial wall and lodges the **lacrimal sac**.

questions.text: The naso-lacrimal duct leads from the lacrimal groove to the ___ of the nose.
questions.explanation:
**Completed Sentence:**
The naso-lacrimal duct leads from the lacrimal groove to the **inferior meatus** of the nose.

questions.text: The ___ and ___ foramina lie at the junction of the roof and medial wall.
questions.explanation:
**Completed Sentence:**
The **anterior** and **posterior ethmoidal** foramina lie at the junction of the roof and medial wall.

questions.text: The ___, ___, and ___ transmit the ___ and ___.
questions.explanation:
**Completed Sentence:**
The **infraorbital groove**, **canal**, and **foramen** transmit the **infraorbital nerve** and **vessels**.

questions.text: The ___ passes through the ___ part of the ___ orbital fissure.
questions.explanation:
**Completed Sentence:**
The **superior ophthalmic vein** passes through the **lateral** part of the **superior** orbital fissure.

questions.text: List structures transmitted through inferior orbital fissure.
questions.modelAnswer: a) Infraorbital nerve (Continuation of maxillary nerve).  b) Zygomatic nerve.  c) Orbital branches of the pterygopalatine ganglion. d) Infraorbital vessels. e) Communication between inferior ophthalmic v. and pterygoid plexus of vs.
questions.explanation: Model answer is provided based on the Special Senses syllabus.

questions.text: What is the orbital fascia (periorbital)?
questions.modelAnswer: The periosteum of the bony orbit.
questions.explanation: Model answer is provided based on the Special Senses syllabus.

questions.text: What are the flap-like expansions of the orbital fascia into the eyelids called?
questions.modelAnswer: Orbital septum
questions.explanation: Model answer is provided based on the Special Senses syllabus.

questions.text: Which structures pierce the bulbar fascia?
questions.modelAnswer: 1. Tendons of extraocular muscles 2. Ciliary nerves 3. Ciliary vessels
questions.explanation: Model answer is provided based on the Special Senses syllabus.

questions.text: What is the function of the episcleral space?
questions.modelAnswer: It allows the eyeball to move freely within its sheath.
questions.explanation: Model answer is provided based on the Special Senses syllabus.

questions.text: Describe the structure and position of the suspensory ligament of the eyeball.
questions.modelAnswer: A hammock-like expansion of the bulbar fascia located below the eyeball.
questions.explanation: Model answer is provided based on the Special Senses syllabus.

questions.text: Posteriorly, the orbital fascia is continuous with the ___ and the ___.
questions.explanation:
**Completed Sentence:**
Posteriorly, the orbital fascia is continuous with the **dura mater** and the **sheath of the optic nerve**.

questions.text: Anteriorly, the orbital fascia is continuous with the ___ at the orbital margin.
questions.explanation:
**Completed Sentence:**
Anteriorly, the orbital fascia is continuous with the **periosteum** at the orbital margin.

questions.text: The bulbar fascia (fascial sheath) extends from the ___ to the ___.
questions.explanation:
**Completed Sentence:**
The bulbar fascia (fascial sheath) extends from the **optic nerve** to the **sclerocorneal junction (limbus)**.

questions.text: The bulbar fascia is separated from the ___ by the ___.
questions.explanation:
**Completed Sentence:**
The bulbar fascia is separated from the **sclera** by the **episcleral space**.

questions.text: The bulbar fascia forms ___ that cover each orbital muscle.
questions.explanation:
**Completed Sentence:**
The bulbar fascia forms **tubular sheaths** that cover each orbital muscle.

questions.text: The ___ is a triangular expansion from the ___ attached to the ___.
questions.explanation:
**Completed Sentence:**
The **medial check ligament** is a triangular expansion from the **medial rectus sheath** attached to the **medial wall of the orbit**.

questions.text: The ___ is a triangular expansion from the ___ attached to the ___.
questions.explanation:
**Completed Sentence:**
The **lateral check ligament** is a triangular expansion from the **lateral rectus sheath** attached to the **lateral wall of the orbit**.

questions.text: List the 7 voluntary muscles of the eye
questions.modelAnswer: 1. Superior rectus (SR) 2. Inferior rectus (IR) 3. Medial rectus (MR) 4. Lateral rectus (LR) 5. Superior oblique (SO) 6. Inferior oblique (IO) 7. Levator palpebrae superioris (LPS)
questions.explanation: Model answer is provided based on the Special Senses syllabus.

questions.text: Where do the four recti muscles insert?
questions.modelAnswer: Into the sclera, anterior to the equator of the eyeball (posterior to the limbus).
questions.explanation: Model answer is provided based on the Special Senses syllabus.

questions.text: Where do the two oblique muscles insert?
questions.modelAnswer: Into the sclera, posterior to the equator of the eyeball.
questions.explanation: Model answer is provided based on the Special Senses syllabus.

questions.text: What are the three attachment points for the Levator palpebrae superioris (LPS) tendon?
questions.modelAnswer: 1. Skin of the upper eyelid 2. Superior tarsus (Muller's muscle) 3. Superior fornix of the conjunctiva
questions.explanation: Model answer is provided based on the Special Senses syllabus.

questions.text: What are the three axes of eyeball movement?
questions.modelAnswer: 1. Transverse (elevation/depression) 2. Vertical (adduction/abduction) 3. Anteroposterior (intorsion/extorsion)
questions.explanation: Model answer is provided based on the Special Senses syllabus.

questions.text: Define "intorsion" of the eyeball
questions.modelAnswer: Movement of the upper rim (12 o'clock position) of the cornea toward the nose.
questions.explanation: Model answer is provided based on the Special Senses syllabus.

questions.text: What is the primary action of the Medial Rectus (MR)?
questions.modelAnswer: Adduction
questions.explanation: Model answer is provided based on the Special Senses syllabus.

questions.text: What is the primary action of the Lateral Rectus (LR)?
questions.modelAnswer: Abduction
questions.explanation: Model answer is provided based on the Special Senses syllabus.

questions.text: What are the three actions of the Superior Rectus (SR)?
questions.modelAnswer: 1. Elevation 2. Adduction 3. Intorsion
questions.explanation: Model answer is provided based on the Special Senses syllabus.

questions.text: What are the three actions of the Inferior Rectus (IR)?
questions.modelAnswer: 1. Depression 2. Adduction 3. Extorsion
questions.explanation: Model answer is provided based on the Special Senses syllabus.

questions.text: What are the three actions of the Superior Oblique (SO)?
questions.modelAnswer: 1. Depression 2. Abduction 3. Intorsion
questions.explanation: Model answer is provided based on the Special Senses syllabus.

questions.text: What are the three actions of the Inferior Oblique (IO)?
questions.modelAnswer: 1. Elevation 2. Abduction 3. Extorsion
questions.explanation: Model answer is provided based on the Special Senses syllabus.

questions.text: List the three intraocular muscles
questions.modelAnswer: 1. Constrictor pupillae 2. Dilator pupillae 3. Ciliaris
questions.explanation: Model answer is provided based on the Special Senses syllabus.

questions.text: The four recti arise from the ___.
questions.explanation:
**Completed Sentence:**
The four recti arise from the **common annular tendon (common tendinous ring)**.

questions.text: The common annular tendon attaches laterally to the ___ and medially to the ___.
questions.explanation:
**Completed Sentence:**
The common annular tendon attaches laterally to the **superior orbital fissure** and medially to the **optic canal**.

questions.text: The recti form a muscular cone where the apex is the ___ and the base is the ___.
questions.explanation:
**Completed Sentence:**
The recti form a muscular cone where the apex is the **common tendinous ring** and the base is the **muscle insertions**.

questions.text: The ___ muscle passes through a fibro-cartilaginous pulley called the ___.
questions.explanation:
**Completed Sentence:**
The **Superior oblique** muscle passes through a fibro-cartilaginous pulley called the **trochlea**.

questions.text: The ___ muscle originates from the  ___.
blanks: floor of the orbit on the maxilla
questions.explanation:
**Completed Sentence:**
The **Inferior oblique** muscle originates from the  **floor of the orbit on the maxilla**.

questions.text: The ___ muscle is the smooth involuntary part of the Levator Palpebrae Superiosis and is supplied by ___ fibers.
questions.explanation:
**Completed Sentence:**
The **Muller's** muscle is the smooth involuntary part of the Levator Palpebrae Superiosis and is supplied by **sympathetic** fibers.

questions.text: The ___ division of the ___ nerve supplies the SR and LPS.
questions.explanation:
**Completed Sentence:**
The **Superior** division of the **oculomotor** nerve supplies the SR and LPS.

questions.text: The ___ division of the ___ nerve supplies the MR, IR, and IO.
questions.explanation:
**Completed Sentence:**
The **Inferior** division of the **oculomotor** nerve supplies the MR, IR, and IO.

questions.text: The Superior Oblique (SO) is supplied by the ___ nerve.
questions.explanation:
SO4

**Completed Sentence:**
The Superior Oblique (SO) is supplied by the **trochlear** nerve.

questions.text: The Lateral Rectus (LR) is supplied by the ___ nerve.
questions.explanation:
LR6

**Completed Sentence:**
The Lateral Rectus (LR) is supplied by the **abducent** nerve.

questions.text: ___ of the eyeball is a combined action of the ___ and ___.
questions.explanation:
**Completed Sentence:**
**Elevation** of the eyeball is a combined action of the **Superior Rectus (SR)** and **Inferior Oblique (IO)**.

questions.text: ___ of the eyeball is a combined action of the ___ and ___.
questions.explanation:
**Completed Sentence:**
**Depression** of the eyeball is a combined action of the **Inferior Rectus (IR)** and **Superior Oblique (SO)**.

questions.text: Adduction of eye is performed by the ___ or the combined action of the ___ and ___.
questions.explanation:
**Completed Sentence:**
Adduction of eye is performed by the **MR alone** or the combined action of the **SR** and **IR**.

questions.text: Abduction of eye is performed by the ___ or the combined action of the ___ and ___.
questions.explanation:
**Completed Sentence:**
Abduction of eye is performed by the **LR alone** or the combined action of the **SO** and **IO**.

questions.text: Intorsion is a combined action of the ___ and ___.
questions.explanation:
**Completed Sentence:**
Intorsion is a combined action of the **SO** and **SR**.

questions.text: Extorsion is a combined action of the ___ and ___.
questions.explanation:
**Completed Sentence:**
Extorsion is a combined action of the **IO** and **IR**.

questions.text: The ___ muscle is supplied by ___ nerves and accommodates the lens for ___ vision.
questions.explanation:
**Completed Sentence:**
The **Ciliaris** muscle is supplied by **parasympathetic** nerves and accommodates the lens for **near** vision.

questions.text: The ___ pupillae is supplied by parasympathetic nerves, while the ___ pupillae is supplied by sympathetic nerves.
questions.explanation:
**Completed Sentence:**
The **Constrictor** pupillae is supplied by parasympathetic nerves, while the **Dilator** pupillae is supplied by sympathetic nerves.

questions.text: List the 5 components of the lacrimal apparatus
questions.modelAnswer: 1. Lacrimal gland and its ducts 2. Conjunctival sac 3. Lacrimal puncti and lacrimal canaliculi 4. Lacrimal sac 5. Nasolacrimal duct
questions.explanation: Model answer is provided based on the Special Senses syllabus.

questions.text: What are the two parts of the lacrimal gland?
questions.modelAnswer: 1. Orbital part (larger and deeper) 2. Palpebral part (smaller and superficial)
questions.explanation: Model answer is provided based on the Special Senses syllabus.

questions.text: Where is the orbital part of the lacrimal gland located?
questions.modelAnswer: In the lacrimal fossa
questions.explanation: Model answer is provided based on the Special Senses syllabus.

questions.text: Where is the palpebral part of the lacrimal gland located?
questions.modelAnswer: In the upper eyelid
questions.explanation: Model answer is provided based on the Special Senses syllabus.

questions.text: Where are the accessory lacrimal glands located?
questions.modelAnswer: In the conjunctival fornices
questions.explanation: Model answer is provided based on the Special Senses syllabus.

questions.text: What is the arterial supply of the lacrimal gland?
questions.modelAnswer: Lacrimal branch of the ophthalmic artery
questions.explanation: Model answer is provided based on the Special Senses syllabus.

questions.text: What two types of fibers are contained within the lacrimal nerve?
questions.modelAnswer: 1. Sensory 2. Secretomotor
questions.explanation: Model answer is provided based on the Special Senses syllabus.

questions.text: Define palpebral conjunctiva
questions.modelAnswer: The mucous membrane lining the deep surface of the eyelids
questions.explanation: Model answer is provided based on the Special Senses syllabus.

questions.text: Define bulbar conjunctiva
questions.modelAnswer: The mucous membrane lining the front of the eyeball
questions.explanation: Model answer is provided based on the Special Senses syllabus.

questions.text: What is the conjunctival sac?
questions.modelAnswer: The potential space between the palpebral and bulbar conjunctiva
questions.explanation: Model answer is provided based on the Special Senses syllabus.

questions.text: What structures form the superior and inferior fornices of the eye?
questions.modelAnswer: The lines of reflection between the palpebral and bulbar conjunctiva
questions.explanation: Model answer is provided based on the Special Senses syllabus.

questions.text: Where are the lacrimal puncti located?
questions.modelAnswer: On the medial end of the lid margin
questions.explanation: Model answer is provided based on the Special Senses syllabus.

questions.text: What is the anatomical relationship between the lacrimal sac and the medial palpebral ligament?
questions.modelAnswer: The lacrimal sac is situated behind the medial palpebral ligament
questions.explanation: Model answer is provided based on the Special Senses syllabus.

questions.text: Describe the superior and inferior ends of the lacrimal sac
questions.modelAnswer: Superior end: Blind Inferior end: Continuous with the nasolacrimal duct
questions.explanation: Model answer is provided based on the Special Senses syllabus.

questions.text: The lacrimal gland ducts (approximately ___ in number) pierce the conjunctiva of the ___ lid.
questions.explanation:
**Completed Sentence:**
The lacrimal gland ducts (approximately **12** in number) pierce the conjunctiva of the **upper** lid.

questions.text: The secretomotor fibers for lacrimation begin in the ___ nucleus, which is located in the ___.
questions.explanation:
**Completed Sentence:**
The secretomotor fibers for lacrimation begin in the **lacrimatory** nucleus, which is located in the **lower pons**.

questions.text: Preganglionic parasympathetic fibers for lacrimation travel via the ___ nerve and then the ___ nerve.
questions.explanation:
**Completed Sentence:**
Preganglionic parasympathetic fibers for lacrimation travel via the **facial** nerve and then the **greater superficial petrosal** nerve.

questions.text: The nerve of the pterygoid canal carries fibers to relay in the ___ ganglion.
questions.explanation:
**Completed Sentence:**
The nerve of the pterygoid canal carries fibers to relay in the **pterygopalatine** ganglion.

questions.text: Postganglionic secretomotor fibers pass from the pterygopalatine ganglion into the ___ nerve, then the ___ nerve.
questions.explanation:
**Completed Sentence:**
Postganglionic secretomotor fibers pass from the pterygopalatine ganglion into the **zygomatic** nerve, then the **zygomatico-temporal** nerve.

questions.text: The final communication to the lacrimal gland occurs via a branch from the ___ nerve to the ___ nerve.
questions.explanation:
**Completed Sentence:**
The final communication to the lacrimal gland occurs via a branch from the **zygomatico-temporal** nerve to the **lacrimal** nerve.

questions.text: The conjunctival sac opens out at the ___.
questions.explanation:
**Completed Sentence:**
The conjunctival sac opens out at the **palpebral fissure**.

questions.text: Each lacrimal punctum leads to a ___, which opens into the ___.
questions.explanation:
**Completed Sentence:**
Each lacrimal punctum leads to a **lacrimal canaliculus**, which opens into the **lacrimal sac**.

questions.text: What is the embryological origin of the optic nerve fibers?
questions.modelAnswer: Axons of the ganglionic layer of the retina
questions.explanation: Model answer is provided based on the Special Senses syllabus.

questions.text: Why is the optic nerve considered a tract rather than a peripheral nerve?
questions.modelAnswer: It has no neurilemmal sheath (cannot regenerate) and is enclosed in 3 meningeal sheaths
questions.explanation: Model answer is provided based on the Special Senses syllabus.

questions.text: List the three parts of the optic nerve and their respective lengths
questions.modelAnswer: 1. Intra-orbital: 25 mm 2. Intra-canalicular: 5 mm 3. Intra-cranial: 10 mm
questions.explanation: Model answer is provided based on the Special Senses syllabus.

questions.text: What structure lies between the optic nerve and the tendon of the lateral rectus?
questions.modelAnswer: Ciliary ganglion
questions.explanation: Model answer is provided based on the Special Senses syllabus.

questions.text: Which vessels and nerves cross the optic nerve in the orbit?
questions.modelAnswer: 1. Ophthalmic artery 2. Nasociliary nerve 3. Superior ophthalmic vein
questions.explanation: Model answer is provided based on the Special Senses syllabus.

questions.text: What is the smallest division of the trigeminal nerve?
questions.modelAnswer: Ophthalmic nerve (V1)
questions.explanation: Model answer is provided based on the Special Senses syllabus.

questions.text: List the three main branches of the Ophthalmic nerve (V1)
questions.modelAnswer: 1. Lacrimal (smallest) 2. Frontal (largest) 3. Nasociliary (intermediate)
questions.explanation: Model answer is provided based on the Special Senses syllabus.

questions.text: Which nerve provides secretomotor fibers to the lacrimal gland?
questions.modelAnswer: Zygomatico-temporal nerve (via a communication to the lacrimal nerve)
questions.explanation: Model answer is provided based on the Special Senses syllabus.

questions.text: What are the two terminal branches of the frontal nerve?
questions.modelAnswer: 1. Supratrochlear nerve (small, medial) 2. Supraorbital nerve (large, lateral)
questions.explanation: Model answer is provided based on the Special Senses syllabus.

questions.text: Which muscles are supplied by the superior division of the Oculomotor nerve (CN III)?
questions.modelAnswer: 1. Superior rectus (SR) 2. Levator palpebrae superioris (LPS)
questions.explanation: Model answer is provided based on the Special Senses syllabus.

questions.text: Which muscles are supplied by the inferior division of the Oculomotor nerve (CN III)?
questions.modelAnswer: 1. Medial rectus (MR) 2. Inferior rectus (IR) 3. Inferior oblique (IO)
questions.explanation: Model answer is provided based on the Special Senses syllabus.

questions.text: What are the clinical signs of a complete Oculomotor (CN III) nerve palsy?
questions.modelAnswer: 1. Ptosis 2. Lateral squint (unopposed LR/SO) 3. Dilated pupil (mydriasis) 4. Loss of accommodation 5. Diplopia
questions.explanation: Model answer is provided based on the Special Senses syllabus.

questions.text: What is the unique superficial attachment of the Trochlear nerve (CN IV)?
questions.modelAnswer: The dorsal aspect of the brain stem (below inferior colliculus)
questions.explanation: Model answer is provided based on the Special Senses syllabus.

questions.text: What is the clinical presentation of Trochlear nerve (CN IV) damage?
questions.modelAnswer: Diplopia (double vision) when looking downwards
questions.explanation: Model answer is provided based on the Special Senses syllabus.

questions.text: What is the superficial attachment of the Abducent nerve (CN VI)?
questions.modelAnswer: Medial part of the lower border of the pons
questions.explanation: Model answer is provided based on the Special Senses syllabus.

questions.text: What is the clinical result of Abducent nerve (CN VI) paralysis?
questions.modelAnswer: Medial (internal) squint
questions.explanation: Model answer is provided based on the Special Senses syllabus.

questions.text: Where is the ciliary ganglion located?
questions.modelAnswer: Near the apex of the orbit, between the optic nerve and lateral rectus
questions.explanation: Model answer is provided based on the Special Senses syllabus.

questions.text: What are the three roots of the ciliary ganglion?
questions.modelAnswer: 1. Motor (Parasympathetic) 2. Sensory 3. Sympathetic
questions.explanation: Model answer is provided based on the Special Senses syllabus.

questions.text: Which nerve provides the motor (parasympathetic) root to the ciliary ganglion?
questions.modelAnswer: The nerve to the inferior oblique (from CN III)
questions.explanation: Model answer is provided based on the Special Senses syllabus.

questions.text: What structures are supplied by the short ciliary nerves?
questions.modelAnswer: 1. Sphincter pupillae 2. Ciliaris muscle 3. Blood vessels of the eyeball
questions.explanation: Model answer is provided based on the Special Senses syllabus.

questions.text: The optic nerve pierces the sclera about ___ medial to the posterior pole of the eyeball.
questions.explanation:
**Completed Sentence:**
The optic nerve pierces the sclera about **3 mm** medial to the posterior pole of the eyeball.

questions.text: The intra-orbital part of the optic nerve is ___ to allow for free movement of the eyeball.
questions.explanation:
**Completed Sentence:**
The intra-orbital part of the optic nerve is **tortuous** to allow for free movement of the eyeball.

questions.text: The central artery and vein of the retina pierce the optic nerve about ___ behind the eyeball.
questions.explanation:
**Completed Sentence:**
The central artery and vein of the retina pierce the optic nerve about **1.25 cm** behind the eyeball.

questions.text: In the optic canal, the optic nerve lies ___ to the ophthalmic artery.
questions.explanation:

questions.text: What is the pupillary response in a patient with a left-sided afferent defect?

questions.text: What is the difference between the direct and consensual light reflex?

questions.text: What is the specific visual field defect associated with a temporal lobe lesion?

questions.text: What is the specific visual field defect associated with a parietal lobe lesion?
questions.modelAnswer: "Pie in the floor" (Lower quadrantanopia)

questions.modelAnswer: Crossed homonymous hemianopia with macular sparing

questions.text: What are the two destinations of optic nerve fibers?
questions.modelAnswer: 1. Lateral geniculate body (80% - Visual fibers) 2. Pretectal area (20% - Pupillary fibers)

questions.text: What is the definition of optic atrophy?
questions.modelAnswer: Death of optic nerve fibers from the ganglion cells to the lateral geniculate body
questions.explanation: Model answer is provided based on the Special Senses syllabus.

questions.text: What are the classic symptoms of acute optic neuritis?
questions.modelAnswer: 1. Rapid/marked vision deterioration 2. Defective color vision ("washed out") 3. Periocular pain (especially with eye movement)
questions.explanation: Model answer is provided based on the Special Senses syllabus.

questions.text: Why does retrobulbar neuritis cause pain during eye movement?
questions.modelAnswer: The origins of the medial and superior rectus muscles are attached to the dural sheath of the optic nerve
questions.explanation: Model answer is provided based on the Special Senses syllabus.

questions.text: What are the fundus findings in retrobulbar neuritis vs. papillitis?
questions.modelAnswer: Retrobulbar: No abnormal signs (normal fundus) Papillitis: Swollen disc, obliterated cup, hyperemia, inflammatory cells in vitreous
questions.explanation: Model answer is provided based on the Special Senses syllabus.

questions.text: What is the characteristic visual field defect in optic neuritis?
questions.modelAnswer: Central or centrocecal scotoma

questions.text: What are the symptoms of increased intracranial pressure (ICP) leading to papilledema?
questions.modelAnswer: 1. Headache (worse with straining/lying down) 2. Projectile vomiting 3. Amaurosis fugax (transient obscuration of vision)
questions.explanation: Model answer is provided based on the Special Senses syllabus.

questions.text: Compare the laterality of Papillitis vs. Papilledema
questions.modelAnswer: Papillitis: Usually unilateral Papilledema: Bilateral
questions.explanation: Model answer is provided based on the Special Senses syllabus.

questions.text: Compare the pupillary reaction in Papillitis vs. Papilledema
questions.modelAnswer: Papillitis: Afferent pupillary defect (APD) Papilledema: Normal pupillary reaction
questions.explanation: Model answer is provided based on the Special Senses syllabus.

questions.text: Compare the vitreous findings in Papillitis vs. Papilledema
questions.modelAnswer: Papillitis: Dust-like opacities (inflammatory cells) Papilledema: Normal vitreous
questions.explanation: Model answer is provided based on the Special Senses syllabus.

questions.text: The swinging-flashlight test should be conducted in a ___ room.

questions.text: Early stages of papilledema produce an ___ on visual field testing.
questions.explanation:

Early stages of papilledema produce an **enlargement of the blind spot** on visual field testing.

questions.text: Ischemic optic neuropathy typically presents with an ___ visual field defect.
questions.explanation:

Ischemic optic neuropathy typically presents with an **altitudinal** visual field defect.

questions.text: Optic nerve fibers become myelinated and covered by meninges once they enter the ___.
questions.explanation:

Optic nerve fibers become myelinated and covered by meninges once they enter the **orbit**.

questions.text: Primary optic atrophy is characterized by a ___ disc with ___ edges.
questions.explanation:
**Completed Sentence:**
Primary optic atrophy is characterized by a **milky white** disc with **well-defined** edges.

questions.text: Secondary optic atrophy is characterized by a ___ disc with ___ edges.
questions.explanation:
**Completed Sentence:**
Secondary optic atrophy is characterized by a **grayish white** disc with **ill-defined** edges.

questions.text: Consecutive optic atrophy presents with a ___ disc and ___ vessels.
questions.explanation:
**Completed Sentence:**
Consecutive optic atrophy presents with a **yellow waxy** disc and **markedly attenuated** vessels.

questions.text: Glaucomatous optic atrophy is characterized by a ___ cup and ___ of the vessels.

Glaucomatous optic atrophy is characterized by a **deep** cup and **nasal shift** of the vessels.

questions.text: Optic neuritis usually affects the age group of ___ years.
questions.explanation:
**Completed Sentence:**
Optic neuritis usually affects the age group of **20 to 40** years.

questions.text: In ischemic optic neuropathy, fundus examination reveals a ___ disc.
questions.explanation:

In ischemic optic neuropathy, fundus examination reveals a **pale** disc.

questions.text: In chronic papilledema, the optic disc may take on a ___ or ___ shape.

questions.text: Visual Evoked Potential (VEP) is ___ in papillitis but ___ in papilledema.

questions.text: In early papilledema, there is an absence of ___ (SVP).

In early papilledema, there is an absence of **spontaneous venous pulsation** (SVP).

questions.text: The optic nerve fibers leave the eye by passing through the ___ of the sclera.

The optic nerve fibers leave the eye by passing through the **lamina cribrosa** of the sclera.

questions.text: In papillitis, the pupillary reaction to direct light is ___ and ___.
questions.explanation:
**Completed Sentence:**
In papillitis, the pupillary reaction to direct light is **sluggish** and **ill-sustained**.

questions.text: The visual field defect in optic radiation lesions can range from ___ to ___.
questions.explanation:
**Completed Sentence:**
The visual field defect in optic radiation lesions can range from **quadrantanopia** to **complete crossed homonymous hemianopia**.

questions.text: The sensory innervation of the lateral auricle is provided by the ___ nerve (upper 2/3) and the ___ nerve (lower 1/3).

questions.text: The sensory innervation of the medial auricle is provided by the ___ nerve (upper 2/3) and the ___ nerve (lower 1/3).

questions.text: The root of the auricle is innervated by the ___ nerve.

questions.text: The external auditory meatus is approximately ___ in total length.

The external auditory meatus consists of an outer **cartilaginous** part (8 mm) and an inner **bony** part (16 mm).

questions.text: The skin of the external auditory meatus contains ___ and ___ (waxy) glands.

questions.text: In newborns, the external auditory meatus is ___ and ___ (lacks constriction).

questions.text: The ___ (branch of facial nerve) passes between the fibrous and mucosal layers of the tympanic membrane.

questions.text: The anterior wall of the middle ear contains openings for the ___ muscle and the ___.
questions.explanation:

The anterior wall of the middle ear contains openings for the **tensor tympani** muscle and the **auditory (Eustachian) tube**.

questions.text: The ___ on the medial wall of the middle ear is caused by the ___.

The **promontory** on the medial wall of the middle ear is caused by the **basal turn of the cochlea**.

questions.text: The ___ muscle originates from the pyramid and inserts into the ___.

The **stapedius** muscle originates from the pyramid and inserts into the **neck of the stapes**.

The **tensor tympani** muscle is supplied by the **mandibular** nerve (CN V3).

questions.text: The ___ muscle is supplied by the ___ nerve (CN VII).

The **stapedius** muscle is supplied by the **facial** nerve (CN VII).

questions.text: The ___ is located on the ___ of the medial wall.

questions.text: The pharyngotympanic tube consists of a posterior 1/3 that is ___ and an anterior 2/3 that is ___.

questions.text: What is the unique structural feature of the auditory pathway compared to most other sensory pathways?

questions.text: Third-order auditory fibers pass through the ___ of the ___ to synapse in the medial geniculate body (MGB).

questions.text: The ___ nucleus sends fibers via the greater petrosal nerve to relay in the ___ ganglion.
questions.explanation:
**Completed Sentence:**
The **Lacrimatory** nucleus sends fibers via the greater petrosal nerve to relay in the **pterygopalatine** ganglion.

questions.text: The ___ nucleus provides postganglionic parasympathetic fibers to the glands of the ___.
questions.explanation:
**Completed Sentence:**
The **Uncertain** nucleus provides postganglionic parasympathetic fibers to the glands of the **palate, pharynx, and nose**.

questions.text: The Nucleus Solitarius (SVA) receives taste from the anterior 2/3 of the tongue via the ___ and from the soft palate via the ___.
questions.explanation:

The Nucleus Solitarius (SVA) receives taste from the anterior 2/3 of the tongue via the **chorda tympani** and from the soft palate via the **greater petrosal nerve**.

questions.text: General sensation from the external ear is carried to the ___.
questions.explanation:

General sensation from the external ear is carried to the **Spinal Nucleus of Trigeminal (V)**.

questions.text: The facial nerve emerges from the brain at the ___ (lower border of pons).
questions.explanation:
**Completed Sentence:**
The facial nerve emerges from the brain at the **cerebellopontine angle** (lower border of pons).

questions.text: The nervus intermedius emerges between the ___ (medial) and the ___ (lateral).
questions.explanation:
**Completed Sentence:**
The nervus intermedius emerges between the **motor root** (medial) and the **vestibulocochlear nerve (CN VIII)** (lateral).

questions.text: The facial nerve enters the bony facial canal at the fundus of the ___.
questions.explanation:
**Completed Sentence:**
The facial nerve enters the bony facial canal at the fundus of the **internal acoustic meatus**.

questions.text: The facial nerve exits the skull through the ___ foramen.
questions.explanation:
**Completed Sentence:**
The facial nerve exits the skull through the **stylomastoid** foramen.

questions.text: The greater petrosal nerve joins the ___ nerve to form the ___ (Vidian nerve).
questions.explanation:
**Completed Sentence:**
The greater petrosal nerve joins the **deep petrosal** nerve to form the **nerve of pterygoid canal** (Vidian nerve).

questions.text: The chorda tympani arises ___ above the stylomastoid foramen and joins the ___ nerve.
questions.explanation:
**Completed Sentence:**
The chorda tympani arises **6 mm** above the stylomastoid foramen and joins the **lingual** nerve.

questions.text: A lesion ___ to the geniculate ganglion results in loss of taste, hyperacusis, and impaired lacrimation.
questions.explanation:
**Completed Sentence:**
A lesion **proximal** to the geniculate ganglion results in loss of taste, hyperacusis, and impaired lacrimation.

questions.text: ___ (abnormally loud sounds) occurs in facial nerve lesions due to paralysis of the ___ muscle.
questions.explanation:
**Completed Sentence:**
**Hyperacusis** (abnormally loud sounds) occurs in facial nerve lesions due to paralysis of the **stapedius** muscle.

questions.text: In a Lower Motor Neuron (LMN) lesion, ___ muscles of the ___ half of the face are affected.
questions.explanation:
**Completed Sentence:**
In a Lower Motor Neuron (LMN) lesion, **all** muscles of the **ipsilateral** half of the face are affected.

questions.text: The most common cause of a facial nerve supranuclear lesion (UMNL) is ___ in the ___.
questions.explanation:
**Completed Sentence:**
The most common cause of a facial nerve supranuclear lesion (UMNL) is **hemorrhage** in the **internal capsule**.

questions.text: The greater superficial petrosal nerve passes through its hiatus in the petrous temporal bone to reach the ___ cranial fossa, passing below the ___ ganglion.
questions.explanation:
**Completed Sentence:**
The greater superficial petrosal nerve passes through its hiatus in the petrous temporal bone to reach the **middle** cranial fossa, passing below the **trigeminal** ganglion.

questions.text: The temporal branch of the facial nerve supplies the ___ and ___ muscles.
questions.explanation:
**Completed Sentence:**
The temporal branch of the facial nerve supplies the **frontalis** and **orbicularis oculi** muscles.

questions.text: The posterior auricular nerve supplies the ___ of the occipitofrontalis muscle.
questions.explanation:
**Completed Sentence:**
The posterior auricular nerve supplies the **occipital belly** of the occipitofrontalis muscle.

questions.text: What is the Medial Longitudinal Fasciculus (MLF)?

questions.explanation: Model answer is provided based on the Special Senses syllabus.

questions.text: Which cranial nerve nuclei are connected by the MLF to facilitate eye movement?
questions.modelAnswer: 1. Oculomotor (CN III) 2. Trochlear (CN IV) 3. Abducent (CN VI)

questions.text: Which specific nucleus does the MLF connect to for head/neck movement?
questions.modelAnswer: Spinal nucleus of accessory nerve (CN XI)

questions.text: What are the two primary functions of the Medial Longitudinal Fasciculus?
questions.modelAnswer: 1. Coordinated eyeball and head movements (in response to vestibulo-cochlear stimuli) 2. Pathway for conjugate lateral eye movements

questions.text: The Medial Longitudinal Fasciculus extends upwards to the ___ in the ___.

questions.text: The Medial Longitudinal Fasciculus continues inferiorly into the spinal cord as the ___.

The Medial Longitudinal Fasciculus continues inferiorly into the spinal cord as the **medial vestibulospinal tract**.

questions.text: The Medial Longitudinal Fasciculus connects the ___ nuclei with the motor nuclei of CN III, IV, VI, and XI.

The Medial Longitudinal Fasciculus connects the **vestibular and cochlear** nuclei with the motor nuclei of CN III, IV, VI, and XI.

questions.text: In the pathway for conjugate lateral eye movements, the MLF connects the ___ nucleus of one side with the ___ nucleus of the opposite side.

In the pathway for conjugate lateral eye movements, the MLF connects the **abducent (VI)** nucleus of one side with the **oculomotor (III)** nucleus of the opposite side.

questions.text: The Medial Longitudinal Fasciculus coordinates movements of the eyeball and head in response to ___ stimuli.
questions.explanation:
**Completed Sentence:**
The Medial Longitudinal Fasciculus coordinates movements of the eyeball and head in response to **vestibulo-cochlear** stimuli.

questions.text: The vestibular nerve enters the posterior cranial fossa and passes through the ___ to reach the brain stem.
questions.explanation:

The vestibular nerve enters the posterior cranial fossa and passes through the **cerebellopontine angle** to reach the brain stem.

questions.text: Vestibulo-cerebellar fibers reach the cerebellum through the ___.
questions.explanation:
**Completed Sentence:**
Vestibulo-cerebellar fibers reach the cerebellum through the **inferior cerebellar peduncle (ICP)**.

questions.text: Vestibulo-cerebellar fibers end specifically in the ___ lobe of the cerebellum.
questions.explanation:
**Completed Sentence:**
Vestibulo-cerebellar fibers end specifically in the **flocculonodular** lobe of the cerebellum.

questions.text: The Medial Longitudinal Bundle (MLB) connects vestibular nuclei with the nuclei of cranial nerves ___, ___, and ___.
questions.explanation:
**Completed Sentence:**
The Medial Longitudinal Bundle (MLB) connects vestibular nuclei with the nuclei of cranial nerves **III**, **IV**, and **VI**.

questions.text: Vestibular impulses relay in the ___ nucleus of the thalamus before reaching the cortex.
questions.explanation:
**Completed Sentence:**
Vestibular impulses relay in the **VPM (ventral posteromedial)** nucleus of the thalamus before reaching the cortex.

questions.text: A tumor arising from the ___ cells in the ___ sheath of CN VIII is a common cause of cerebellopontine angle lesions.

A tumor arising from the **Schwann** cells in the **neurilemmal** sheath of CN VIII is a common cause of cerebellopontine angle lesions.

questions.text: The vestibular reflex allows for fixation of the eyes on an object while the head moves in the ___ direction.

The vestibular reflex allows for fixation of the eyes on an object while the head moves in the **opposite** direction.

questions.text: The vestibular nerve passes through the ___ alongside the facial nerve.

The vestibular nerve passes through the **internal auditory meatus** alongside the facial nerve.

questions.text: What are the three main anatomical divisions of the ear?
questions.modelAnswer: 1. External ear 2. Middle ear 3. Inner ear
questions.explanation: Model answer is provided based on the Special Senses syllabus.

questions.text: What type of cartilage forms the ear pinna?
questions.modelAnswer: Yellow elastic fibro-cartilage
questions.explanation: Model answer is provided based on the Special Senses syllabus.

questions.text: What tissue composes the lobule of the ear?
questions.modelAnswer: Adipose connective tissue (covered by thin skin)
questions.explanation: Model answer is provided based on the Special Senses syllabus.

questions.text: What is the primary function of the tympanic membrane?
questions.modelAnswer: To transmit sound waves to the bony ossicles of the middle ear.
questions.explanation: Model answer is provided based on the Special Senses syllabus.

questions.text: List the three auditory ossicles in order from the tympanic membrane to the inner ear.
questions.modelAnswer: 1. Malleus 2. Incus 3. Stapes
questions.explanation: Model answer is provided based on the Special Senses syllabus.

questions.text: What is the function of the auditory ossicles?
questions.modelAnswer: They act as a lever to magnify vibrations and conduct them to the inner ear.
questions.explanation: Model answer is provided based on the Special Senses syllabus.

questions.text: What is the function of the Eustachian (auditory) tube?
questions.modelAnswer: To equalize pressure in the middle ear with the atmospheric pressure in the nasopharynx.
questions.explanation: Model answer is provided based on the Special Senses syllabus.

questions.text: What are the three components of the bony labyrinth?
questions.modelAnswer: 1. Cochlea 2. Vestibule 3. Semicircular canals
questions.explanation: Model answer is provided based on the Special Senses syllabus.

questions.text: What are the three components of the membranous labyrinth?
questions.modelAnswer: 1. Cochlear duct 2. Utricle and saccule 3. Membranous semicircular canals
questions.explanation: Model answer is provided based on the Special Senses syllabus.

questions.text: What is the sensory organ for hearing?
questions.modelAnswer: Organ of Corti
questions.explanation: Model answer is provided based on the Special Senses syllabus.

questions.text: What are the sensory organs for equilibrium?
questions.modelAnswer: 1. Maculae (of utricle and saccule) 2. Crista ampullaris (of semicircular canals)
questions.explanation: Model answer is provided based on the Special Senses syllabus.

questions.text: What is the function of the Stapedius muscle?
questions.modelAnswer: It pulls the stapes out to protect the organ of Corti from high vibrations.
questions.explanation: Model answer is provided based on the Special Senses syllabus.

questions.text: The external auditory meatus consists of an outer ___ that is ___ and an inner ___ that is ___.
questions.explanation:
**Completed Sentence:**
The external auditory meatus consists of an outer **one third** that is **cartilaginous** and an inner **two thirds** that is **bony**.

questions.text: Ceruminous glands in the external auditory meatus are modified ___.
questions.explanation:
**Completed Sentence:**
Ceruminous glands in the external auditory meatus are modified **apocrine sweat glands**.

questions.text: The middle ear is an air-filled space located in the ___ part of the ___ bone.
questions.explanation:
**Completed Sentence:**
The middle ear is an air-filled space located in the **petrous** part of the **temporal** bone.

questions.text: The middle ear communicates posteriorly with the ___ and anteriorly with the ___.
questions.explanation:
**Completed Sentence:**
The middle ear communicates posteriorly with the **mastoid air sinus** and anteriorly with the **Eustachian (auditory) tube**.

questions.text: The ___ (anterior) is closed by the foot plate of the stapes, while the ___ (posterior) is closed by an elastic membrane.
questions.explanation:
**Completed Sentence:**
The **oval window** (anterior) is closed by the foot plate of the stapes, while the **round window** (posterior) is closed by an elastic membrane.

questions.text: The auditory ossicles are covered by ___ epithelium and articulate by ___ joints.
questions.explanation:
**Completed Sentence:**
The auditory ossicles are covered by **simple squamous** epithelium and articulate by **synovial** joints.

questions.text: The middle ear cavity is lined by ___ epithelium that is strongly adherent to the underlying ___.
questions.explanation:
**Completed Sentence:**
The middle ear cavity is lined by **simple cubical** epithelium that is strongly adherent to the underlying **periosteum**.

questions.text: The ___ muscle inserts into the malleus to make the ear drum tense.
questions.explanation:
**Completed Sentence:**
The **Tensor tympani** muscle inserts into the malleus to make the ear drum tense.

questions.text: In the Eustachian tube, simple cuboidal epithelium is gradually replaced by ___ epithelium with ___.
questions.explanation:
**Completed Sentence:**
In the Eustachian tube, simple cuboidal epithelium is gradually replaced by **ciliated pseudostratified columnar** epithelium with **goblet cells**.

questions.text: The bony labyrinth is filled with ___, which is similar to extracellular fluid but with ___ content.
questions.explanation:
**Completed Sentence:**
The bony labyrinth is filled with **perilymph**, which is similar to extracellular fluid but with **lower protein** content.

questions.text: The membranous labyrinth is filled with ___.
questions.explanation:
**Completed Sentence:**
The membranous labyrinth is filled with **endolymph**.

questions.text: The Organ of Corti is located specifically within the ___.
questions.explanation:
**Completed Sentence:**
The Organ of Corti is located specifically within the **cochlear duct**.

questions.text: The Maculae of the ___ and ___ are responsible for equilibrium.
questions.explanation:
**Completed Sentence:**
The Maculae of the **utricle** and **saccule** are responsible for equilibrium.

questions.text: The ___ is the sensory organ located in the semicircular canals.
questions.explanation:
**Completed Sentence:**
The **Crista ampullaris** is the sensory organ located in the semicircular canals.

questions.text: What is the central part of the bony labyrinth?
questions.modelAnswer: The vestibule
questions.explanation: Model answer is provided based on the Special Senses syllabus.

questions.text: What structures are contained within the membranous labyrinth of the vestibule?
questions.modelAnswer: The utricle and saccule
questions.explanation: Model answer is provided based on the Special Senses syllabus.

questions.text: What duct connects the utricle and the saccule?
questions.modelAnswer: The utriculosaccular duct
questions.explanation: Model answer is provided based on the Special Senses syllabus.

questions.text: What is the specific name for the receptor areas of the utricle and saccule?
questions.modelAnswer: The maculae
questions.explanation: Model answer is provided based on the Special Senses syllabus.

questions.text: List the three components of the maculae neuroepithelium
questions.modelAnswer: 1. Hair cells 2. Supporting cells 3. Nerve endings
questions.explanation: Model answer is provided based on the Special Senses syllabus.

questions.text: What is the characteristic shape of Type I hair cells?
questions.modelAnswer: Flask-shaped (rounded base, narrow apex)
questions.explanation: Model answer is provided based on the Special Senses syllabus.

questions.text: What is the characteristic shape of Type II hair cells?
questions.modelAnswer: Cylindrical
questions.explanation: Model answer is provided based on the Special Senses syllabus.

questions.text: What is the "cuticular plate" in vestibular hair cells?
questions.modelAnswer: An actin-rich region of apical cytoplasm that returns stereocilia to an upright position
questions.explanation: Model answer is provided based on the Special Senses syllabus.

questions.text: List the two primary functions of the maculae supporting cells
questions.modelAnswer: 1. Support and nutrition of hair cells 2. Production of the otolithic membrane
questions.explanation: Model answer is provided based on the Special Senses syllabus.

questions.text: What are otoliths (otoconia) composed of?
questions.modelAnswer: Calcium carbonate crystals
questions.explanation: Model answer is provided based on the Special Senses syllabus.

questions.text: List the three semicircular canals
questions.modelAnswer: 1. Superior 2. Posterior 3. Lateral
questions.explanation: Model answer is provided based on the Special Senses syllabus.

questions.text: What is the name of the expanded end of each semicircular canal?
questions.modelAnswer: The ampulla
questions.explanation: Model answer is provided based on the Special Senses syllabus.

questions.text: What is the receptor area located in the ampulla of the semicircular ducts?
questions.modelAnswer: The crista ampullaris
questions.explanation: Model answer is provided based on the Special Senses syllabus.

questions.text: What is the central bony column around which the cochlea turns?
questions.modelAnswer: The modiolus
questions.explanation: Model answer is provided based on the Special Senses syllabus.

questions.text: What is the "osseous spiral lamina"?
questions.modelAnswer: A bony shelf extending laterally from the modiolus
questions.explanation: Model answer is provided based on the Special Senses syllabus.

questions.text: What structure forms the roof of the cochlear duct?
questions.modelAnswer: The vestibular membrane (Reissner's membrane)
questions.explanation: Model answer is provided based on the Special Senses syllabus.

questions.text: What structure forms the floor of the cochlear duct?
questions.modelAnswer: The basilar membrane
questions.explanation: Model answer is provided based on the Special Senses syllabus.

questions.text: What is the spiral limbus?
questions.modelAnswer: The periosteal connective tissue covering the osseous spiral lamina
questions.explanation: Model answer is provided based on the Special Senses syllabus.

questions.text: Contrast the arrangement of stereocilia in Inner vs. Outer hair cells
questions.modelAnswer: Inner: Linear array Outer: V-shape bundles
questions.explanation: Model answer is provided based on the Special Senses syllabus.

questions.text: Which type of cochlear hair cell is more heavily innervated?
questions.modelAnswer: Inner hair cells
questions.explanation: Model answer is provided based on the Special Senses syllabus.

questions.text: List the collagen types found in the tectorial membrane
questions.modelAnswer: Types II, V, IX, and XI
questions.explanation: Model answer is provided based on the Special Senses syllabus.

questions.text: What structure is formed by the separation of the inner and outer pillar cells?
questions.modelAnswer: The inner tunnel of Corti
questions.explanation: Model answer is provided based on the Special Senses syllabus.

questions.text: What is the specific function of Outer Phalangeal cells?
questions.modelAnswer: They support the base of outer hair cells with cup-shaped apices
questions.explanation: Model answer is provided based on the Special Senses syllabus.

questions.text: The utricle and saccule are lined by ___ epithelium.
questions.explanation:
**Completed Sentence:**
The utricle and saccule are lined by **simple squamous** epithelium.

questions.text: Type I hair cells are completely surrounded by afferent nerve terminals called a ___.
questions.explanation:
**Completed Sentence:**
Type I hair cells are completely surrounded by afferent nerve terminals called a **calyx**.

questions.text: Type II hair cells are associated with ___ endings from afferent nerves.
questions.explanation:
**Completed Sentence:**
Type II hair cells are associated with **bouton** endings from afferent nerves.

questions.text: The apical border of a vestibular hair cell contains ___ kinocilium and ___ stereocilia.
questions.explanation:
**Completed Sentence:**
The apical border of a vestibular hair cell contains **one** kinocilium and **30-50** stereocilia.

questions.text: The ___ is the conical proteoglycan layer of the crista ampullaris which ___ otoliths.
questions.explanation:
**Completed Sentence:**
The **cupula** is the conical proteoglycan layer of the crista ampullaris which **lacks** otoliths.

questions.text: The cochlea turns upon itself ___ times.
questions.explanation:
**Completed Sentence:**
The cochlea turns upon itself **2.5 (or 2 ¾)** times.

questions.text: The ___ is the membranous labyrinth of the cochlea and contains ___.
questions.explanation:
**Completed Sentence:**
The **scala media** is the membranous labyrinth of the cochlea and contains **endolymph**.

questions.text: The scala vestibuli and scala tympani communicate at the apex of the cochlea via the ___.
questions.explanation:
**Completed Sentence:**
The scala vestibuli and scala tympani communicate at the apex of the cochlea via the **helicotrema**.

questions.text: The scala tympani communicates with the middle ear through the ___.
questions.explanation:
**Completed Sentence:**
The scala tympani communicates with the middle ear through the **round window**.

questions.text: The ___ is a stratified epithelium containing an intraepithelial plexus of ___.
questions.explanation:
**Completed Sentence:**
The **stria vascularis** is a stratified epithelium containing an intraepithelial plexus of **capillaries**.

questions.text: The ___ is responsible for the production and maintenance of ___.
questions.explanation:
**Completed Sentence:**
The **stria vascularis** is responsible for the production and maintenance of **endolymph**.

questions.text: The basilar membrane contains ___ fibers and supports the organ of Corti.
questions.explanation:
**Completed Sentence:**
The basilar membrane contains **keratin-like** fibers and supports the organ of Corti.

questions.text: The ___ membrane is an acellular structure secreted by cells of the ___.
questions.explanation:
**Completed Sentence:**
The **tectorial** membrane is an acellular structure secreted by cells of the **spiral limbus**.

questions.text: Unlike vestibular hair cells, cochlear hair cells have ___.
questions.explanation:
**Completed Sentence:**
Unlike vestibular hair cells, cochlear hair cells have **no kinocilium**.

questions.text: The apical ends of phalangeal cells are joined to hair cells by ___.
questions.explanation:
**Completed Sentence:**
The apical ends of phalangeal cells are joined to hair cells by **tight junctions**.

questions.text: The vestibular membrane consists of two layers of ___ epithelium separated by their ___.
questions.explanation:
**Completed Sentence:**
The vestibular membrane consists of two layers of **squamous** epithelium separated by their **basement membranes**.

**Completed Sentence:**
In salt transduction, \( \ce{Na+} \) depolarizes the taste cell by entering through **leakage channels**.

questions.text: Sour substances (acids) depolarize taste cells by ___ or ___.
questions.explanation:
**Completed Sentence:**
Sour substances (acids) depolarize taste cells by **entering through Na+ channels** or **blocking K+ channels**.

questions.text: Sweet substances bind to metabotropic receptors to stimulate the production of ___, which leads to the ___ or ___.
questions.explanation:
**Completed Sentence:**
Sweet substances bind to metabotropic receptors to stimulate the production of **cAMP**, which leads to the **opening of Na+ channels** or **closing of K+ channels**.

questions.text: Bitter and Umami substances act on metabotropic receptors to stimulate the production of ___, which increases ___ levels.
questions.explanation:
**Completed Sentence:**
Bitter and Umami substances act on metabotropic receptors to stimulate the production of **IP3**, which increases **intracellular Ca2+** levels.

questions.text: Olfactory receptor cells are ___ nerve cells with distal ends forming a knob with ___ cilia.
questions.explanation:
**Completed Sentence:**
Olfactory receptor cells are **bipolar** nerve cells with distal ends forming a knob with **6-12** cilia.

questions.text: In olfactory transduction, the odorant-OBP complex activates ___, which increases ___.
questions.explanation:
**Completed Sentence:**
In olfactory transduction, the odorant-OBP complex activates **adenyl cyclase**, which increases **cAMP**.

questions.text: During olfaction, the opening of cation channels allows an inward current of ___ (and Na+), which subsequently opens ___.
questions.explanation:
**Completed Sentence:**
During olfaction, the opening of cation channels allows an inward current of **\( \ce{Ca^2+} \)** (and Na+), which subsequently opens **\( \ce{Cl-} \)-activated channels**.

questions.text: In olfactory neurons, depolarization is unique because ___ leaves the cell due to high intracellular concentrations.
questions.explanation:
**Completed Sentence:**
In olfactory neurons, depolarization is unique because **\( \ce{Cl-} \)** leaves the cell due to high intracellular concentrations.

questions.text: The mechanism of adaptation in smell involves the extrusion of \( \ce{Ca^2+} \) via the ___.
questions.explanation:
**Completed Sentence:**
The mechanism of adaptation in smell involves the extrusion of \( \ce{Ca^2+} \) via the **\( \ce{Na+/Ca^2+} \) exchanger**.

**Anosmia** refers to the total loss of the sensation of smell.

questions.text: If no clear cause for anosmia is found, ___ or ___ of the head is performed to rule out structural abnormalities (e.g., tumors or fractures).
